verdict.rationale: Ramp documents its own rules-based automation in several places. Procurement workflows route requests automatically by vendor type, spend category, or dollar amount. Notification workflows trigger on spend amount or team role, and cards auto-lock when compliance is unmet. A configurable human-in-the-loop policy auto-approves routine spend, and in-policy expenses are auto-approved. However, these are fixed, domain-specific triggers described in one-line marketing claims, not a general event-to-action rule builder. Webhooks only notify external systems and are a building block, so they earn no credit here. Missing for 10: a general user-defined trigger/condition/action rule engine, in-depth docs on rule configuration and the events and actions available, independent or hands-on corroboration.
